title: Dolma: Deduplication documentation
authors: Allen Institute for AI / Dolma contributors
supports: In-memory Bloom tagging can classify documents or paragraphs as duplicates; mixer subsequently drops them; false positives are acknowledged.
limitations: Moving main branch; motivates application only. We did not benchmark Dolma or claim its implementation maintains our exact authoritative log.

title: Distinct Sampling for Highly-Accurate Answers to Distinct Values Queries and Event Reports
inspected_passages: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, printed pages 544 onward / PDF page 4
supports: Occurrence sampling favors frequent values; hash-consistent sampling can sample distinct IDs with bounded storage. Our bottom-k baseline belongs to this established family.
limitations: Its level-based implementation and query-estimation objective differ from our simple bottom-k auditing use; no claim of identical end-to-end application.

title: Mitigating False Positives in Filters: To Adapt or to Cache?
venue: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 51(3), Article 17
inspected_passages: Indexed primary publisher abstract, metadata, and Introduction
supports: Direct modern predecessor for adaptation versus caching under Zipfian and network workloads; explicitly requires an oracle identifying false positives.
limitations: Direct open returned an internal error on one attempt; primary publisher indexed text supplied abstract and complete visible introduction. Detailed algorithm limitation is additionally supported by the accessible 2021 full text.

title: Mitigating False Positives in Filters: to Adapt or to Cache?
inspected_passages: Introduction page 2 on serendipitous false-positive corrections
supports: Broom fingerprint repair can eliminate other future false positives; backing dictionary supplies a colliding stored element, whose access is accounted for asymptotically in that setting.
limitations: Not implemented here. Ordinary-Bloom idempotence and min(B,U) scoped oracle bounds do not cover collateral corrections from these adaptive representations.

title: Approximately Detecting Duplicates for Streaming Data using Stable Bloom Filters
inspected_passages: Introduction and URL crawling motivating example, PDF page 1
supports: Approximate stream deduplication and the possibility of missed new URLs under limited resources are established applications; stable filters evict old information.
limitations: Not the same model: our exact processed log persists and our insert-only Bloom does not evict entries. No quantitative SBF guarantee was reused.

title: Minimizing Regret With Label Efficient Prediction
inspected_passages: Sections I and II, PDF pages 1–2
supports: Learning from a bounded number of paid outcome observations is an established problem with regret bounds.
limitations: Adjacent prior art, not a theorem directly subsuming mutable deduplication: processing changes future membership labels and our loss counts distinct retained documents.

title: LSHBloom: Internet-Scale Text Deduplication
supports: Current probabilistic document-deduplication research evaluates memory/runtime/accuracy and configurable Bloom false-positive overhead. A generic Bloom-for-corpus use is not a novelty claim.
limitations: Near-duplicate LSH problem differs from our exact-ID audit allocation. HTML title differs from arXiv metadata title; placeholder PVLDB DOI in source does not establish publication. We did not validate all of its mathematical claims.
